risk-treatment.hint: Drag each decision onto the treatment option it represents. Ask what happened to the risk itself, not how much work the response took.
risk-treatment.note: Treatment answers 'what are we doing about this risk'. It is a different axis from control strength, which answers 'how effective is the reduction'. Buying insurance is a strong treatment decision and no control at all.
risk-treatment.zones[0].def: Do not undertake, or stop undertaking, the activity that gives rise to the risk. The exposure goes to zero because the activity goes to zero.
risk-treatment.zones[1].def: Keep the activity but act on likelihood or impact. Most controls live here, and residual risk always remains.
risk-treatment.zones[2].def: Move the financial or legal consequence to another party. The hazard is untouched; only who pays changes.
risk-treatment.zones[3].def: Retain the risk knowingly, at the level of authority entitled to accept it, and record the decision.

rt-01.label: After a risk assessment, the company cancels its planned emotion-recognition feature for workplace monitoring entirely.
rt-01.why: The activity itself is abandoned, so the exposure disappears rather than being managed. Avoidance is the only treatment that removes a risk instead of shrinking it.

rt-02.label: A vendor's model would require processing biometric data the firm has no lawful basis for, so the firm withdraws from the procurement.
rt-02.why: Declining to proceed is a treatment decision, not the absence of one. It is usually the right answer when the risk is unacceptable at any residual level.

rt-03.label: A bank decides not to deploy an automated decisioning model in the one jurisdiction where it could not meet the contestability requirement.
rt-03.why: Scoping the activity out of a jurisdiction removes the exposure there. Partial avoidance by scope is still avoidance.

rt-04.label: A team drops a planned feature that would have inferred health status from purchase history, judging no mitigation sufficient.
rt-04.why: When no control brings residual risk within tolerance, avoidance is the remaining option. The tell is that the activity stops, not that it is watched more closely.

rt-05.label: Confidence thresholds are introduced so that uncertain cases are routed to a trained reviewer instead of being auto-decided.
rt-05.why: The activity continues with lower likelihood of an unreviewed wrong decision. Residual risk remains — reviewers are fallible — which is the signature of reduction.

rt-06.label: The training corpus is rebalanced and the model is re-evaluated by subgroup before release.
rt-06.why: This lowers the probability of disparate performance without eliminating it. Measurable improvement with residual exposure is reduction, not avoidance.

rt-07.label: Rate limits, output filters and a kill switch are added to a customer-facing assistant.
rt-07.why: Each measure attacks likelihood or impact while the service keeps running. Note that the kill switch reduces impact rather than likelihood — both count.

rt-08.label: Model cards, evaluation results and known limitations are published so deployers can use the system within its tested envelope.
rt-08.why: Reducing misuse by informing the deployer is a genuine, if weak, reduction. Its weakness is a control-strength question, not a treatment classification one.

rt-09.label: The firm buys specific AI liability insurance covering claims arising from automated decisions.
rt-09.why: The financial consequence moves to the insurer while the model behaves exactly as before. Insurance never reduces the probability of harm and is not a control.

rt-10.label: A contract makes the model vendor liable for damages caused by defects in the supplied system.
rt-10.why: Contractual indemnity reallocates cost between parties. The affected individual is no better protected, which is why regulators do not treat it as mitigation.

rt-11.label: A high-risk processing activity is outsourced to a specialist provider under a contract making them responsible for compliance failures.
rt-11.why: Outsourcing shifts operational and financial consequence, though rarely regulatory accountability — a distinction that catches people out.

rt-12.label: The deployer negotiates a warranty and a capped indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from generated output.
rt-12.why: The exposure is priced and shifted rather than diminished. A cap means the transfer is partial, which is worth recording in the risk register.

rt-13.label: A small residual risk of a low-severity formatting error is documented, signed off by the product owner, and reviewed annually.
rt-13.why: Informed, authorised and recorded retention is acceptance. Acceptance is a decision with an owner and a review date, not silence.

rt-14.label: The risk committee records that the residual risk of the deployment is within stated appetite and no further action is required this cycle.
rt-14.why: Explicit retention at the authority entitled to retain it. If nobody at the right level said yes, the risk is not accepted — it is merely unmanaged.

rt-15.label: A known limitation with a documented workaround is scheduled for review at the next model refresh rather than being fixed now.
rt-15.why: Time-boxed retention with a review point is acceptance. The workaround does not make it reduction, because the risk itself is unchanged in the meantime.

rt-16.label: The board notes that the cost of further mitigation exceeds the expected loss and directs that the residual risk be retained and monitored.
rt-16.why: A cost-justified retention decision at board level, with monitoring attached. Monitoring is not a control here — it detects, it does not prevent.
